description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/backend.rs:125-194

```rust
/// Return all FileNode IDs in the subtree rooted at any node in
/// `root_ids`, up to `max_depth` levels deep (0 = direct children
/// only, `u64::MAX` = full subtree).
fn query_subtree(...) -> Result<Vec<Id>, Self::Error> { ... }
```

The doc says "0 = direct children only" but the default impl
(lines 148-194) does:

```rust
let mut depth_remaining = max_depth;
loop {
    if frontier.is_empty() || depth_remaining == 0 {
        break;
    }
    depth_remaining = depth_remaining.saturating_sub(1);
    ...
}
```

When `max_depth = 0`, the loop breaks before the first `query_objects`
call. The function returns `Ok(vec![])` — empty descendants. That
contradicts the doc which says "0 = direct children only".

Compare the handler:
`crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/filenode.rs:902`:
```rust
let depth: u64 = args.get("depth").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0);
...
if depth == 0 {
    return Ok((response, tail));   // flat result, no subtree
}
```

The handler treats `depth == 0` as "no subtree expansion at all" and
short-circuits before even calling `query_subtree`. So the trait's
"0 = direct children only" claim is contradicted by both the default
impl and the only call site.

Two interpretations diverge silently:

1. **`depth = 0` means "skip subtree entirely"** — what the handler
   and default impl actually do.
2. **`depth = 0` means "direct children only"** — what the doc says.

A backend implementor reading the doc and writing their own override
will pick (2) — and produce results that the handler does not expect.
The handler short-circuits before calling, so the implementor's
return value never reaches the response, but the impl will likely
have built up a query path for the (2) interpretation that goes
unused — wasted work, silent inconsistency.

Also separately: the contract for max_depth = u64::MAX is documented
as "full subtree", but the default impl uses `saturating_sub(1)`
inside a `loop` that breaks on `depth_remaining == 0`. For
u64::MAX, the loop runs 2^64 times until frontier empties OR
depth_remaining wraps to 0. On a pathological tree with deep
branching this is reachable; on a real tree it is fine. Worth
documenting the practical cap.

Suggested fix: pick one of:

a) Align the doc with the impl: "depth = 0 returns no descendants;
   depth = N returns up to N levels of children, N >= 1 includes
   direct children."
b) Align the impl with the doc: rebase the loop so `max_depth = 0`
   returns the direct children, `max_depth = 1` includes grandchildren,
   etc. Update the handler's `if depth == 0` short-circuit
   accordingly.

Either is fine; the current state (doc and impl disagree) is the bug.

`api-contract,underspecified` because the contract is documented
but the documentation contradicts the implementation. Implementors
will pick the wrong interpretation and ship a backend whose
output the handler discards.
title: FileNodeBackend::query_subtree default impl: caller can never tell whether 0-depth means 'no children' or 'depth=0 requested'
